name: Acute Stress Disorder Scale — supplied COVID-19 version
directions: The supplied form asks about recent feelings related to COVID-19. Rate each item from 1 (not at all) to 5 (very much). This COVID-19-framed version is not presented as the original validated ASDS or as a diagnosis.

questions.text: Have you felt numb or distant from your emotions?
Have you ever felt in a daze?
Have things around you ever felt unreal or dreamlike?
Have you ever felt distant from your normal self, as if watching it happen from outside?
Have you been unable to recall important aspects of things that happened?
Have memories of things that happened kept entering your mind?
Have you had bad dreams or nightmares?
Have you felt as if you were reliving things that happened?
Do you feel very upset when reminded of things that happened?
Have you tried not to think about it?
Have you tried not to talk about it?
Have you tried to avoid situations or people that remind you of it?
Have you tried not to feel upset or distressed about it?
Have you had trouble sleeping?
Have you felt more irritable?
Have you had difficulty concentrating?
Have you become more alert to danger?
Have you become jumpy?
When you think about it, do you sweat or tremble or does your heart beat fast?
Thinking about all these reactions together, how much are they bothering you or getting in the way of work, relationships or other parts of life?

attribution: Supplied source cites Bryant R, Moulds M, Guthrie R. Acute Stress Disorder Scale: a self-report measure of acute stress disorder. Psychol Assess. 2000;12(1):61–68. This supplied form is COVID-19-framed.
